heard: Up to 2,500 people vanished in a single fiery night. Severe drought gripped Wisconsin on October 8, 1871. A cold front created winds reaching 110 miles per hour. The blaze reached 2,000 degrees Fahrenheit and vaporized entire forests. Father Peter Pernin survived by immersing himself in the freezing river. This remains the deadliest wildfire in all of American history. Chicago erupted 400 miles south that same night, casting these victims into shadow.
